label: START B5
title: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and no ACE inhibitor
statement: Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (ACE) inhibitor for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: For heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, review whether an ACE inhibitor is suitable. A patient taking sacubitril with valsartan or an ARB documented as the appropriate alternative has no ACE inhibitor omission. An ACE inhibitor must not be combined with sacubitril with valsartan.

medicine_groups.name: ACE inhibitors (medicines that meet this criterion)
medicine_groups.note: Coversyl Plus is perindopril with indapamide. Coveram is perindopril with amlodipine. Triapin is ramipril with felodipine. Zestoretic is lisinopril with hydrochlorothiazide. Accuretic is quinapril with hydrochlorothiazide. Tarka is trandolapril with verapamil. Combination products count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Angiotensin receptor blockers and sacubitril with valsartan are not ACE inhibitors and are not listed. Triasyn contains ramipril with felodipine.

medicine_groups.name: Medicines that imply the condition
medicine_groups.note: Ivabradine is used for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Eplerenone is used for it and after a heart attack, so it implies the condition less strongly.

medicine_groups.name: Alternatives to review
medicine_groups.note: Use this group only to identify an alternative for review. Confirm that Entresto is current or that the ARB is current and documented as the appropriate alternative for heart failure before closing the omission. A brand or a combination tablet alone does not establish its purpose.

needs_facts.what: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
needs_facts.meets: The record documents heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, or documents heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less. If only a low ejection fraction is documented, ask whether heart failure has been diagnosed. Use Not known if heart failure is established but its type is unclear.

Enter the measured left ventricular ejection fraction in percent and its measurement date if known. A value of 40% or less supports reduced function in a person with confirmed heart failure. A percentage alone cannot establish heart failure.

needs_facts.what: Treatment for heart failure when an ACE inhibitor appears absent
needs_facts.meets: Check identifiable supplies first. In an otherwise possible omission, clarify an outside ACE inhibitor supply or the current use or purpose of a possible alternative. A confirmed qualifying treatment explains the omission. If none applies, assess the remaining clinical facts. An unknown answer leaves the treatment question open.

options.words: Currently taking an angiotensin receptor blocker documented as the appropriate alternative for heart failure

needs_facts.what: Reason an ACE inhibitor was withheld after a reaction
needs_facts.meets: Ask only if reported cough or swelling leaves it unclear whether a clinician advises avoiding ACE inhibitors now. A documented current reason explains the omission. If there is no current restriction, assess the remaining facts. Symptoms of uncertain significance need clinical review.

options.words: A clinician documented a reaction as the current reason to avoid an ACE inhibitor
No current restriction due to a reaction
Previous cough or swelling, but its significance is unclear

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 years or older. If age is unknown, confirm it before reporting a finding. If the person is taking sacubitril with valsartan (Entresto), or an ARB documented as the appropriate alternative for heart failure, there is no ACE inhibitor omission. Read identifiable supplies first. If an otherwise possible omission depends on a reported outside supply or an alternative whose use or purpose is unclear, name "Treatment for heart failure when an ACE inhibitor appears absent". A confirmed outside ACE inhibitor supply in the review period or either appropriate alternative closes the omission. If none applies, assess the other facts. If the treatment is unknown, keep the finding possible. Suspect a finding when Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is documented and no Group A medicine was supplied in the last six months of the record. Cite the diagnosis line. Confirmed heart failure with a measured left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less also qualifies. Cite both lines when they establish the subtype together. When neither route confirms the diagnosis but a Group B medicine is supplied and no Group A medicine is supplied in the last six months, report only a possible finding and cite a Group B supply. If the diagnosis is unclear, name "Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction" and ask whether heart failure has been diagnosed. A low ejection fraction alone also prompts this possible finding if the omission otherwise fits. It does not diagnose heart failure. With heart failure confirmed but reduced function uncertain, name "Left ventricular ejection fraction" only for an otherwise possible finding. Use the dated result if available. An unknown value cannot confirm reduced function. If reported cough or swelling leaves the reason for withholding treatment unclear, keep the finding possible and name "Reason an ACE inhibitor was withheld after a reaction". A documented current reason to avoid an ACE inhibitor explains the omission. With no current restriction, assess the remaining facts. A past symptom of uncertain significance needs clinical review. When a Group A medicine is supplied in the last six months, or heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is ruled out, there is no finding.
cannot_be_seen: The true ejection fraction, past ACE inhibitor cough or swelling, kidney function and potassium, and whether an angiotensin receptor blocker or sacubitril with valsartan is used instead. Also heart failure not on the record.
ask_the_gp: Whether an ACE inhibitor should be started, or the reason it is not suitable.
